method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents' (published 19 September 2023), 25 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC10556443). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086) 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)' (published online 23 June 2020), 10 claims; LICENCE: No licence or reuse terms found on the article pages or in Crossref metadata (treated as all rights reserved); open access journal (DOAJ-listed) (read at the bmhim.com article pages and Crossref records for both DOIs). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, two chapters (puberty blockade; monitoring during treatment) of the Mexican Society of Pediatric Endocrinology 2020 clinical practice guideline, read in Spanish and paraphrased in English, chiefly for GnRH agonist depot doses and success rates (its Table 1 survived HTML extraction), biochemical monitoring and stopping. No Australian CPP guideline was found. The Endocrine Society 2026 guideline is paywalled and the 2019 international consortium update (Karger) is behind a bot challenge (retried 2026-09-24). S1 claims and anchors are unchanged. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from Table 2 (S1 grades of recommendation); S1 Table 3 (GnRH agonist products) has merged cells and was not extracted.

claims.claim: **Precocious puberty means puberty starting before 8 years in girls or before 9 years in boys.**
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep a closer eye on puberty in children with obesity, those born small for gestational age or growth-restricted, and those with a family history of early puberty** (all conditional). In obesity, bone age can run ahead without true puberty, so this must be told apart from CPP.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Measure bone age (strong),** but treat it only as a support: even a bone age more than 2 SD ahead of chronological age does not prove CPP.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A GnRH stimulation test is recommended (strong).** In Korea, a stimulated peak LH above 5 IU/L defines CPP. Triptorelin 0.1 mg can replace LHRH as the stimulus, with the same cut-off, but LH peaks about 3 hours later. ⚠️ Obesity can blunt the LH response, so interpret with care.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnosis rests on the whole picture:** Tanner stage II or more, faster growth velocity and advanced bone age, together with the stimulation test.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A random unstimulated LH on an ultrasensitive assay is a supporting test (conditional):** below 0.3 IU/L suggests prepuberty and above 0.83 IU/L suggests puberty (ICMA method).
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pelvic ultrasound can support the diagnosis in girls (conditional);** in a meta-analysis a uterus of 3.2 cm or longer separated CPP from isolated thelarche with 81.8% sensitivity and 82.0% specificity. **Breast ultrasound is not recommended (strong).**
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Brain MRI:** recommended for every girl with CPP under 6 and for older girls with neurological signs (strong); considered selectively for girls starting puberty at 6–8 years without such signs (conditional); and recommended for boys with CPP (conditional). In girls, MRI abnormalities were found in 25% of those under 6 but 3% of those aged 6 to 8.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Watch for 3 to 6 months first to see how fast puberty is moving (strong):** most suspected cases need no treatment because the development is early or transient.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The treatment decision weighs age, speed of progression, Tanner stage, growth velocity, bone age and loss of predicted adult height.** Slowly progressive puberty typically shows no Tanner-stage change over 6 months or more of observation.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat rapidly progressive precocious puberty (strong).** In a meta-analysis, GnRH agonist therapy added 3.2 cm to adult height on average: about 5.1 cm when started before age 8, but 2.5 cm when started after 8.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Early puberty and slowly progressive puberty are not generally treated,** as untreated adult height is close to mid-parental height. Little height is gained if bone age is already well advanced, and girls treated after age 8 may gain none.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treatment can be considered for girls at high risk of psychosocial distress from early menarche (conditional),** although long-term follow-up has not shown worse adult wellbeing than the general population.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **S2 (Mexico) treats by age at assessment:** a GnRH agonist is recommended for CPP before age 7 in girls or 8 in boys (strong); after those ages, consider it only for a poor adult-height outlook or marked psychosocial impact that counselling alone does not settle, weighing the endocrinologist's judgement and the family's view.
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Height evidence (S2):** in three trials of girls whose puberty began between 7 and 9, GnRH agonists did not change adult height; one high-bias trial in girls under 7 found 4.1 cm more with treatment.
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A GnRH agonist is the standard treatment (strong): leuprolide or triptorelin at the approved dose (strong).** Choose the dosing interval to suit the family, because 4-week and 3-month formulations worked equally well (strong).
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weight-based leuprolide dosing is no longer advised,** for lack of evidence.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not use GnRH antagonists or aromatase inhibitors for CPP (strong):** evidence of benefit is insufficient and neither is approved for it.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Growth hormone added to the agonist is optional (conditional),** for markedly slowed growth or a poor adult-height outlook. Discuss the daily injections and cost with the family first.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **S2: use a depot GnRH agonist, at the lowest dose that suppresses puberty, monthly or quarterly;** heavier children may need more. Follow the maker's preparation instructions (for example, do not shake the vial).
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Leuprorelin depot doses and suppression rates (S2 dose table):** monthly 3.75 mg succeeded in 75–78% and 7.5 mg in 97%; quarterly 11.25 mg in 67–86% (stimulated LH below 4 IU/L), 22.5 mg in 92% and 30 mg in 95–97% (the 30 mg product is not labelled for CPP). Success tends to rise with later doses.
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Triptorelin depot doses and suppression rates (S2 dose table):** 3.75 mg every 28 days, 90–100% at 4 months; 11.25 mg every 84 days, 87.6% at 3 months, 92.8% at 6 and 89.1% at 12; 22.5 mg every 24 weeks, 93.2% at 6 months.
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **If suppression is inadequate (S2),** first confirm adherence and correct preparation and injection, then raise the dose or shorten the interval between injections. Medroxyprogesterone is not recommended for blockade, except as a fallback when no GnRH agonist is available.
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Minor, passing effects do not require stopping (conditional):** headache and hot flushes usually settle. Local reactions such as sterile abscess are uncommon (four of 621, 0.6%, in one Korean study); if they persist, switch formulation. A withdrawal bleed after starting is expected, but bleeding lasting over 2 months needs another explanation.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Assess and treat at once for slipped capital femoral epiphysis, pseudotumour cerebri or anaphylaxis (strong).** SCFE risk is higher with obesity, male sex, a growth spurt or past radiotherapy, so investigate any hip or leg pain.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suppression is not guaranteed (S2):** with leuprorelin, reported failure ranges from 33% (11.25 mg 3-monthly, judged at 3 months) to under 5% (7.5 mg monthly, or 22.5 mg and 30 mg 3-monthly), and failure becomes less common the longer treatment runs.
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Review response every 3 to 6 months (strong), sooner if failure is suspected (conditional).** Effect shows within 2 to 6 months: breast or testicular stage stops advancing and growth slows to prepubertal rates, though pubic hair may still progress with adrenal maturation. Check bone age every 6 months to a year.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Judge failure on the whole picture,** not a single hormone result: progressing Tanner stage and bone age, growth that fails to slow, and unsuppressed hormones together. Thresholds sometimes used (basal LH above 0.6 IU/L, oestradiol above 30 pg/mL, testosterone above 30 ng/dL, stimulated LH above 4 IU/L) are unreliable alone.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **When to stop is individual (conditional).** Adult height benefits most when treatment runs to a bone age of 12–12.5 years (girls) or 13–14 years (boys); continuing in girls past a chronological age of 13 adds nothing. Menarche follows 12 to 18 months after stopping on average, sometimes up to 2 years.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **S2 monitoring schedule:** a clinical and hormonal review (LH, sex steroids) 3 months after the first dose; then clinical review at least every 6 months (Tanner stage, breast diameter or testicular volume, growth velocity, adverse effects, psychosocial impact); bone age at least yearly.
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **S2 hormone checks in girls:** a basal LH below 0.3 IU/L with prepubertal oestradiol and no clinical progression means blockade is working; draw it in the week before the next dose. Do a stimulated LH if there are clinical signs of progression or basal LH is above 0.3 IU/L. **In boys, follow testicular volume;** routine LH stimulation is not recommended.
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **S2 on stopping:** stop when the child is psychosocially ready for puberty and predicted height is near family target height; do not continue beyond age 12 in girls or 14 in boys; follow until puberty is clinically seen to restart.
claims.locator: Sociedad Mexicana de Endocrinología Pediátrica (Torres-Tamayo M, Zurita-Cruz JN, Castilla-Peón MF, et al.), Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México 2020;77(Supl 1):19-25 and 29-35 (doi 10.24875/BMHIM.20000085, 10.24875/BMHIM.20000086), 'Clinical guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of precocious puberty: Puberty blockade; Monitoring during the treatment of precocious puberty (Spanish full text)', published online 23 June 2020, https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-19.html ; https://www.bmhim.com/files/bmhim-77-29.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **After stopping, follow the child until adult height is reached and gonadal function has returned** (menarche in girls).
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Long-term outcomes are reassuring (strong):** GnRH agonist treatment does not impair fertility, raise PCOS risk, or harm metabolic, bone or mental health, so routine long-term surveillance for these is not recommended.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **What S1's grades mean:** a strong 'do' applies to most patients, and a strong 'do not' means most patients should not receive it; a conditional grade means selective use after weighing benefit, harm, cost and the patient's preference, and a conditional 'do not' still allows limited, careful use.
claims.locator: Korean Society of Pediatric Endocrinology (Kim SJ et al.), Annals of Pediatric Endocrinology & Metabolism, '2022 Clinical practice guidelines for central precocious puberty of Korean children and adolescents', published 19 September 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556443/, retrieved 2026-09-23
